macro.regime: Risk-on relief rally meets a hawkish-paused (not pivoted) Fed and early signs of credit stress broadening beyond the distressed CCC tail
macro.narrative: No material shock since Friday's close: Fed-hold odds for the Oct 28 FOMC held near ~82-84% (CME/Kalshi) while December-hike pricing firmed to roughly 65-77%, confirming this is a hawkish pause, not a pivot, following September's hike (the Fed's first since 2023). The 10-year Treasury yield touched ~5.34% intraweek (highest since 2002) before settling ~5.28%; oil held near Brent $102/WTI $91 as Saudi's East-West pipeline begins a slow 6-8 week restart and a third US carrier group still steams toward the Middle East, while Russia kept hitting Kyiv's bridges (a third straight day as of Oct 4) and Germany pledged $1.46B in new aid. The incremental deterioration this run is credit: CCC-and-below OAS pushed further to ~1,215bps (highest since Jan 2023) and broad HY OAS widened from 2.93% to 3.24% over the past week, suggesting the bifurcation story may be starting to broaden beyond the distressed tail. Equities remain propped up almost entirely by the AI-capex trade (Meta capex guidance raised to $145B, Microsoft to $190B, AMD/Nvidia/Arm at highs) with VIX complacent near 15 despite the 24-year-high yield backdrop. Note: a Sept 2 continuing resolution (signed into law, House 370-48) funds the government through Dec 11, 2026, so there is no active shutdown and no shutdown-driven data blackout this week -- this run corrects an earlier draft that had wrongly flagged one; the absence of a CPI print in this week's calendar reflects the normal BLS release schedule, not a shutdown. Net: regime intact, tilt marginally more cautious than Friday on the credit-spread broadening alone.
